PullRequest.Title: Name HydraFusion turns by their Fusion tier under dynamic Auto tiers
PullRequest.Body:
With `chat.copilot.ensemble.enabled` and `chat.copilot.dynamicAutoTiers.enabled` both on, the service offers `hydrafusion` / `hydrafusion-max` as Fusion's own tiers, which drops the `intelligence` tier. `getFusionTierLabel` only labeled HydraFusion through `intelligence`, so it returned nothing. The response footer and the model picker hover then fell back to "HydraFusion" / "HydraFusion Max" instead of "Fusion High" / "Fusion Max".

Changes:
- `getFusionTierLabel`: if Fusion's tier list includes the HydraFusion model id, use that tier's label. This fixes the footer and the picker button.
- Picker hover: name the selected model the way the button does, e.g. "Fusion Max".
- Tabbed picker: a chat on a HydraFusion model is shown on the Fusion tier of the same id. Choosing that tier now moves the chat to Fusion at that tier, as the inline Fusion picker already does, instead of re-selecting the HydraFusion model. `hydrafusion` is also kept as one of Fusion's tiers when the service offers it, so the picker agrees with the button.

With ensemble off (no `autoModelFusion`), none of this applies, and everything still reads HydraFusion / HydraFusion Max.

## How to test

Turn on `chat.copilot.ensemble.enabled` and `chat.copilot.dynamicAutoTiers.enabled`, run a turn on Fusion High or Max, and check the footer and the picker hover. With both settings off, HydraFusion naming is unchanged.

- `./scripts/test.sh --run <all modelPicker/*.test.ts> --run agentHostChatContribution.test.ts`: 1143 passing
- `npm run typecheck-client` and ESLint on the changed files: passed
- Manual, in Code OSS: with both settings off, the picker button shows "HydraFusion · Max" and its hover reads "Models • HydraFusion Max". The footer was checked with both settings on.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render or refresh the model-picker button, hover, tabbed list, and Details card under dynamic Fusion tiers.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Synchronous label/list construction and DOM updates must finish before the picker or label is visible. The changed work is local array/property lookup and formatting; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is reached.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Available model count M for existing scans, plus fixed two HydraFusion IDs and P configuration properties for the changed lookup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread render/refresh; no queue, limiter, or parallel boundary work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The picker reads in-memory model metadata and current configuration. The new Fusion display name is cached as one bounded string on the widget for hover use; cold and warm behavior differ only in existing picker construction, with no new miss retry or negative cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all changed helper calls and render callers were traced and remain in-memory.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The total model catalog varies, but the changed HydraFusion set is fixed at two IDs and provider schema property counts are expected to be small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable render regression: the changed CPU/allocation work is bounded to a tiny provider schema and at most two routing alternatives, and the hover consumes the cached display string rather than rebuilding the catalog.

Scenarios.Scenario: Format Fusion response footers for live turns and restored chat history.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For each rendered/restored response, existing code scans that turn's response parts and calls the changed tier-label helper. The helper adds an in-memory scan of P schema properties before footer text can render.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: H response turns times P provider schema properties; no retained state accumulates.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Footer formatting is synchronous per response; history rendering may call it repeatedly but adds no asynchronous concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Turn metadata and model metadata are already in memory. There is no added cache or boundary lookup; each footer formats from the current metadata.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the state-to-progress and response-details call path was traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: History length H can be large, but provider configuration property count P is small; no evidence shows this lookup dominating existing response-part/history rendering.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the newly added property scan is small, synchronous metadata work with no I/O, fan-out, or retained growth.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choose a provider-backed Fusion tier from the Details card while the chat currently uses the corresponding HydraFusion model.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The added `selectsTier` dispatch enters `_setValues`, which awaits `setModelConfigValues`; for a changed tier this reaches profile-file read/parse/full JSON serialization/save before `_setValues` invokes `onSelect` and the picker switches to Fusion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist Fusion's selected provider tier to the language-model profile configuration file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One profile configuration transaction per changed tier click: existence check/model-reference read, full groups parse/serialization, and one save. Re-selecting the unchanged value avoids the mirrored global write in the scoped store.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Details-card entry followed `_selectVariant`, selected the HydraFusion model synchronously, and did not perform Fusion-tier profile-file persistence on this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The save is awaited before the user-visible model selection callback, so its latency blocks completion of this interaction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One operation per explicit changed tier choice; bytes parsed/serialized scale with all configured language-model provider groups, and rapid same-model choices scale queue wait linearly.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: `SequencerByKey` serializes edits per model. A normal click causes one save; rapid edits for the same Fusion model queue behind one another rather than running concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The chat-scoped configuration store applies the tier locally, then mirrors it to the profile-global language-model configuration. Re-selecting an unchanged value can skip the global write, but a changed value opens/parses and saves the profile file; no coalescing exists beyond per-model sequencing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed branch and complete awaited call chain to `textFileService.save` were traced. A low-severity actionable latency finding was identified, but `report_finding` failed at the tool boundary on three submissions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual delay depends on language-model configuration size and local/profile filesystem latency; the new boundary and await placement are certain, while visible severity is environment-dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity interaction-latency regression: profile persistence was moved onto the model-switch critical path. The finding could not be accepted because the reporting tool returned an execution failure three times.

Scenarios.Scenario: Continue composing or send a chat after moving from HydraFusion to Fusion at the matching provider tier.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After configuration persistence resolves, model selection updates local controller/input state and existing selection persistence. The diff does not add network, IPC, database, or subprocess calls to subsequent chat execution.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected model and one tier per user action.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single selection callback after the per-model configuration sequencer; no burst or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Selection state and the chosen display metadata are in memory after the tier operation; no new network/subprocess cache behavior is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the changed selection dispatch and absence of new downstream boundaries in the inspected call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Existing model-selection persistence internals were not changed; no changed mechanism indicates additional downstream execution cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional performance regression beyond the preceding tier-selection latency; subsequent chat execution paths are unchanged by the diff.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files and all diff pages. Traced picker rendering, hover caching, footer formatting, Details selection, configuration sequencing, and profile filesystem persistence. One low-severity critical-path I/O issue was identified; report_finding failed three times with a generic tool execution error, so no finding was accepted by the endpoint.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
